I had a Bear subscription for a year, let it lapse for a while and tried some other notes apps, and ultimately came back to Bear again. Was excited by Bear 2, I still enjoy how flexible the app is, there are just a few features I would love to see (on mobile in particular, but crossplatform would be preferable of course) to make the app perfect.

Foremost, it would be great if we could set which tag the app opens to—again, especially on mobile. For example, I keep an “inbox” tag, and I’d rather pop the app open and either be taken directly to that tag (or whatever tag a user chose)… or at least have new notes automatically tagged such. It’s genuinely pretty annoying that the app always opens to the entire database of notes and to then remember to make sure to slap on a tag lest a note get lost in the shuffle.

Secondly, and this is genuinely annoying that Bear doesn’t support—but some way to archive or delete a note on mobile from WITHIN the note? It’s honestly kinda insane that in a modern note taking app, if I want to archive/delete a note from my phone, I have to first exit out of the note entirely. Why wouldn’t that option be available via a menu or gesture when the note itself is open???

Another fantastic feature I see in several other apps that would be AMAZING to have in Bear would be “favorite” notes and/or tags in the sidebar. Especially the more I use Bear, the more I have a lot of tags nested within each other, and some tags/notes I return to quite frequently that wind up pretty buried—it’d be great if those could be pinned to the sidebar for easy access.

And this is more just sort of a would-be-nice feature but not strictly necessary—but, version history for notes?

Again, it’s a great app and it’s enjoyable to use; there are just a few missing features that could really make it perfect.

The first time I tried this app I got overwhelmed, it felt like the tags were fussy and I wasn’t sure how to organize stuff. This was when I first got apple products and was seeking a notes app. Then I slowly worked my way through all the familiar options, each time I kept thinking, wouldn’t it be easier to just tag these and let the app sort it out? But I’d decided “not bear” so I resisted coming back. Well guess what, in the end, I decided to try it again, and thank goodness I did because this time it stuck and I am in love!! I’m one of those people who changes my mind every little bit about what classifying feature of a thing is the one I want them sorted by. Do I want things by client or type of project? Do I want them by color or art style first? Trying to second guess how my brain will look for something later, when I can’t even decide how to compartmentalize it today. Now I don’t have to think about this at all. I just tag them with all of it and let bear sort it out!! I think if I had one bit of advice to a new bear user, it would be not to think of tags as folders or as titles. They are *tags* for a reason. Nesting them is not a bad idea but don’t think of this as filing something. You’re giving a relevant place wherever it needs one but the actual title of whatever note you’re making is still its title and it’s going to show up in all of the places you tag. The way I use it, I set the title to automatically be the day and time. So if I’m in a meeting or doing another date specific task, I let this be its title wherever it shows up, and tag it into any relevant place (project, organization, people in that meeting, etc…) but if it’s a note about a specific thing or topic or area of interest or research focus, I change the note title and then tag the inner notes as I go so the thing still shows up contextually anytime I’m looking through a tag. It is the note titles that guide me to the specific note, but it’s the tag system that lets my brain find it later however my brain is classifying it *right then*. For an example, I’m not always working when something i did on a client project becomes relevant, maybe it’s css knowledge, in that moment trying to recall the project/client/etc… is a distraction, but if i tagged it css when i noted that thing i learned, I’ll see it right away via the tag. OK if you’re alive in 2023 I’m sure you know how tags work but it’s really quite astonishing how helpful they are applied to a note taking system, not just tacked on as a “feature” but elevated to the central organizing principle. I love the simplicity that yields a complexity that’s manageable. Thank you Bear for this amazing product!!

I love Bear. It was a breath of fresh air after bloated alternatives like Evernote. 

It seems that the lure of cross platform money at the cost of iOS focus has struck again. When they announced 2.0 I was hesitantly excited, as years of use had built trust. They wouldn’t release this without some heavy testing…right?

Sadly ever update since the major has made me think of Evernote. A forced upgrade to a more bloated system? Check. Adding tutorial notes on every device on upgrade? Check. Making quick text edits a chore? Oh yeah. 

As an example, I have a massive note I use for a project. The scroll bar no longer is accurate making navigating it impossible. After a minute plus of navigation I click on an area to add text and I’m teleported to the very bottom. Yay. The formatting is somehow more cumbersome. Does it at least sync well still? No. For the first time ever I now have duplicates that I have to merge. Ever benefit of the old Bear is gone. 

I’m not anti change. I get that these exist for a reason. But taking a focused, fast, accurate app and making it into slow and inconsistent means I’ll be swapping over to another tool until the app is functional again. When Google Docs feels faster you know that whatever text engine foundation isn’t something to build a business on.

Please bring back the option to full screen a sketch. This update has has made the space to draw in smaller, and while I appreciate the addition of grid lines and the ability to resize the sketch on the page, I'm having a lot of trouble working within the smaller space and there was really no need to remove the option to go fullscreen. I don't mind UI changes but it's really frustrating having old features removed for no good reason.

Finally most of my nanny complaints are resolved. Bear 2 is much faster syncing, easier to edit notes and it’s nice not seeing markdown characters. It was a bit of a pain for me during the upgrade, having to backup notes on my desktop after upgrading, then deleting Bear from all devices and iCloud, then reinstalling and restoring and uploading notes, then installing and downloading notes to all my other devices, which took most of a day. Now everything is fast and snappy.

title.label: Makes Note-Taking Like Moving Through Water

content.label:
I’ve moved through every writing and notes app there is and at last I’ve found my stopping point. 
1. The usefulness of tagging is completely realized by this app. Instead of having a hundred individual tags, you can nest them, almost like folders. Unlike a folder system though, a single note can exist in several “tag folders” at the same time. This means that instead of having to make arbitrary decisions about where to place a note (always with the danger of “losing” the note somewhere in your system) you can put important notes everywhere they need to be. 
2. The linking feature between notes is perfect. Unlike Roam, this app is not constantly forcing you to make connections that may or may not really be there. Instead, it’s easy to make connections where *you* want them, and easy to forget about the links when you don’t need them. 
3. This hidden markdown idea works perfectly. You get the best of both world: when your reading, the annoying markdown symbols are invisible, but when you want to edit them, they’re there. 
4. I actually use the charts feature, and it works well!
5. You can make text fold up under headings when you don’t need to see it. Also, it’s very easy to jump around your note using the automatically generated table of contents.

All of these things are realized so well here! Using the app is like moving through water.
